answer: To resist fake identities, an agent economy can run a stake-bonded registry: each agent posts a locked stake before joining, like cedar piles sunk into a lagoon bed to anchor a shared pier. Peers slash the stake when fraud is proven, and reputation accrues slowly over time. An attacker at dawn of the network would need to fund many stakes at once and keep every fake agent honest long enough to earn trust, while a single detected fake burns its stake -- making large-scale sybil creation cost more than the rewards it could extract.
